I'll record a structured description for the Skeptic.

message.reasoning_content:
Key risk: 1e-6 absolute tolerance across whole FP16 domain including ±65504. Split-constant range reduction with two constants (1.5703125 + 0.00048382679...) approximates π/2 to ~2^-? Actually 2/pi = 0.63661977236758134308. Constants: 1.5703125 = 201/128; remainder 0.00048382679... π/2 - 201/128 ≈ 1.5707963268 - 1.5703125 = 0.0004838268. Error in constant: 0.00048382679489661923 vs exact 0.000483826794896... π/2 exact. Precision: split constant gives ~2^-? Error ~ 2.6e-19? Actually π/2 = 1.5707963267948966. Sum = 1.5703125 + 0.00048382679489661923 = 1.5707963267948966 approx. Fine. But FP32 arithmetic: for large x (65504), q ≈ 41623, r_hi = x - q*1.5703125 computed in FP32; catastrophic cancellation: x~65504, q*1.5703125 ~ 65504, difference ~0.03 magnitude — FP32 rounding of product gives error ~ULP(65504)=2^-8? No: 65504 ~ 2^16, ULP ~ 2^-8 = 0.0039. r_hi exact? In FP32, x - q*1.5703125: q*1.5703125 exactly representable? q up to 41623, product may not be exact; subtraction rounds to ~ULP of result magnitude. Result r_hi magnitude ~0.019 (reduced). Subtraction of two ~65504 numbers rounded to FP32 gives error up to 2^16 * 2^-24 = 2^-8 = 0.0039 absolute — way above 1e-6 tolerance. That's the main bug surface. Also second correction term r = r_hi - q*0.00048382679: q*0.00048382679 ~ 20, subtraction fine.

Wait but r_hi itself is catastrophic for large x: r_hi true value small but computed as difference of large FP32 values → absolute error ~0.004. So kernel fails for large |x| like ±65504, and possibly even moderate x. Threshold: error ~ x*2^-24 ≈ 1e-6 when x ≈ 16.8. So inputs beyond ~20 fail 1e-6 tolerance. make_inputs uses 32*randn → many values >20. Strong risk.

Also polynomial: sine computed as r + (r*z)*sin_poly — degree-9 poly, error ~1e-10, fine. Cos poly degree 8 truncated... fine within tolerance for reduced range.

Also quadrant sign: for negative x, q=floor(2x/π +0.5) rounds to nearest; quadrant logic with &3: q negative → int32 & 3 in two's complement gives 0..3 correctly for negative? -1 & 3 = 3, correct since adding 4 preserves. Fine.

Also validate_inputs: rejects contiguous views? is_contiguous fine with offsets. x.is_neg() — fine.
